messages:
marta: hey team — customer hit a 403 'billing_required' on the Workspace Settings save flow. they provided request id `x-request-id: 0a1b2c3d4e` and said it happened in Chrome 114 on macOS. Can we get repro HAR + console so we can escalate?

support-bot: thanks @marta — please follow the capture checklist below and attach the .har + console text. see also steps to get a curl repro from the failing request.

alex: quick checklist (chrome) — short version: 
1) Open Chrome -> More Tools -> Developer Tools (or ⌥⌘I)
2) Network tab -> check "Preserve log" and "Disable cache"
3) Console tab -> right-click -> "Save as" (or copy all) to capture console output
4) Reproduce the exact user flow (Settings → Billing → Save) while devtools open
5) In Network tab find the failing request (look for 403 and x-request-id header) -> right-click -> "Save all as HAR with content"
6) For the specific request: right-click -> "Copy" -> "Copy as cURL (bash)" and attach that command

Include: browser + version, OS, time (UTC and local), user email (masked) and the x-request-id header value.

marta: great — customer can attach the HAR but asked how to hide tokens/PII.

alex: they should redact Authorization header before sending. two options: 
- in the HAR file plain-text replace the Authorization header value with "REDACTED" (find/replace)
- or attach original HAR privately to support case and mention we will redact on ingestion.
Also ask them to include the cURL so we can hit the same route server-side.

raj: for Safari: 
1) Enable Develop menu (Preferences -> Advanced -> check "Show Develop menu in menu bar")
2) Develop -> Show Web Inspector -> Network tab -> reproduce
3) Right-click on a request -> "Export HAR" (or use 3rd-party HAR exporter if not available)
Note: Safari sometimes omits response bodies; ask the user to paste the response body from Console if possible.

samir: firefox note: Network -> right-click -> "Save All As HAR" includes bodies. Also: about reproducing auth/billing errors, try incognito/private window and disable extensions. Extensions (adblocker/cookie managers) are a common cause of 401/403 differences.

claire: curl repro tips: 
- paste the "Copy as cURL" output and run locally to see auth headers and response.
- if curl returns 403, add -v to get headers: `curl -v '<url>' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'`
- if curl succeeds but browser fails, likely a cookie/CSRFTOKEN or SameSite issue. Please include both responses.

marta: customer provided HAR but says "export failed with error". they attached screenshots of devtools only. any minimal ask we can do while they re-export?

alex: ask them to at least: 
- paste the full failing response body from Console (click XHR -> Response tab -> copy)
- paste the Request/Response headers for the failing call (right-click -> Copy -> Copy response headers)
- include the x-request-id and the browser UTC timestamp for the event

samir: add a short repro script suggestion in case they want to share steps we can run: 
- open an incognito window
- login -> go to /workspace/settings -> change billing details -> click save -> observe 403
- attach exact button clicks (e.g., "Save billing info (card) -> click")

raj: small ops tip — if they can run the cURL and paste both server response headers and body, include `-i` to show headers: `curl -i -X POST '<url>' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d @payload.json`

claire: also useful: mention network conditions. If they have unreliable connectivity, ask them to reproduce with throttling (Chrome DevTools -> Network -> Throttling -> Offline/Slow 3G) so we can see timeout/race conditions.

marta: perfect. I'll ask them to re-export HAR with content, include console log text, the copied cURL, and confirm they redacted tokens. I'll upload the artifacts to the support ticket and paste the thread here. thanks all :pray:

support-bot: checklist summary (paste in reply to customer): 
• Open DevTools (Network + Console) and enable "Preserve log"
• Reproduce the flow, find the failing request (403) and save HAR with content
• Copy the failing request as cURL and run locally if possible (-v or -i flags)
• Save console output and copy response body for the XHR/fetch that 403'd
• Include x-request-id header, browser+version, OS, UTC timestamp, and mask Authorization values
• If using Safari/Firefox, follow the browser-specific export steps above
• Optional: reproduce in incognito and with extensions disabled

marta: attaching the customer's screenshot now — I'll follow up once they re-export. thanks! :thumbsup:
